faq.q: Why does the lunch hall feel so loud?
faq.a: Lots of people talk at once, and hard floors and walls bounce the sound around. Some ears also hear sounds more strongly than others.
asks: Tell me about Too loud for me

faq.q: What helps in a noisy lunch hall?
faq.a: Ear defenders, a seat at the end or by a wall, slow breaths, or eating somewhere quieter if your school allows it.
asks: Tell me about Use a tool

faq.q: What can I say if it is too loud?
faq.a: You can say, It is too loud for me. Can I sit somewhere quieter, please? A grown-up you trust can help.
asks: Tell me about Ask for a seat
Tell me about Tell a grown-up

faq.a: No. They are chatting and having fun. A busy hall is just noisy. It is not about you.

faq.q: Can I eat lunch somewhere else?
faq.a: Some schools have a quiet lunch room or a calm table. Ask your teacher what your school has.
asks: Is there a quiet place to eat?

facts: Hard walls and floors bounce sound around, which makes big halls louder.
Ear defenders lower the loudness of sounds reaching your ears.
